stories.title: Mauricio Pochettino calls for Manchester United to show no fear against Liverpool
summary: New head coach’s first game is at Anfield on Sunday‘We are going there with the idea to win and be brave’Mauricio Pochettino has called on Manchester United to have “no fear” when they travel to Anfield on Sunday for his first game.
The Argentinian does not want his players to take a backward step as he targets a fast start.United are 18th in the Premier League and Liverpool fourth but the head coach will not accept nerves.
Pochettino is known for being attack-minded and will bring those ideals, but will have had only three days with the players since replacing Michael Carrick.

stories.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
summary: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quicklyIt’s injury time at the Emirates on the 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Spurs.

It loops over Manuel Almunia and on to the post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs fans before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans.
Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it.But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport.

summary: There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under-21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García.

The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one.Time to talk, so let’s start with tinseltown, the family tale.
His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing.

stories.title: Inside women’s football’s difficult rise in Syria: ‘A joy that everyone in the country needed’
summary: Today, the first glimmers of hope are beginning to emerge amid difficultyIn December 2024, Syria’s under-18 women’s football team boarded a last-minute bus at midnight from Aqaba, bound for Damascus.
Players from the provinces around Damascus made their way home.

But those from Hasakah, in the country’s far north-east, spent the next three days stranded at Damascus airport, as airline staff fled and planes sat idle on the tarmac, until a bus was finally able to take them home.
